svg.title: How a three level hierarchy is indexed into a flat Copilot index
svg.desc: A Customer to Engagement to TimeEntry hierarchy in SQL Server is flattened by SQL views, which copy each ancestor's searchable text down onto every descendant item and roll descendant names up onto every ancestor item. The result is 1,126 flat external items in Microsoft Graph, each physically containing its ancestors' text, so that a single search for a customer name matches items at all three levels.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Indexing a hierarchy into a flat index

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: A Graph external item has no parent, no children and no join. The traversal is done once, in SQL, and baked into every item's own text.

svg.text: Nothing traverses anything. Every match is a document that already contained the words, decided when it was written rather than when it was asked for.
